stateFields: Comments dictionary entry keyed by policy ID (UserComments / CompComments, CmtxFile.Comments); Nothing when the source has no comment file

states.name: Has a comment
states.writtenAs: policy ID present as a key in the in-memory comment table with non-empty text; reaches the comment file only when the user chooses Save Policies

states.name: No comment
states.writtenAs: policy ID absent from the in-memory comment table (key removed when the text box is emptied; the file drops it only at the next Save Policies)

states.name: Comments unavailable
states.writtenAs: comment table is Nothing for the policy source (no comment path, or loading threw); box disabled with 'Comments unavailable for this policy source', nothing written, nothing saved

statement: We describe the life of the comment table held in memory. A comment reaches the comment file only when the user chooses Save Policies. Errors in that save are ignored, so a comment can silently stay unsaved; a deleted comment leaves the file only then.

assumed.why: The code keeps no flag for saved versus unsaved comments, so the file's state cannot be read from the table.
assumed.ifWrong: If comments were also written to disk on each edit, a saved state would need its own transitions.

evidence.shows: Save Policies writes the comment table; any error is swallowed.
The save builds the whole file from the table and writes it.

statement: Importing a policy settings file sets a comment only when the imported comment is non-empty, so an import never clears a comment. It overwrites existing text. A table that is unavailable is left alone.

evidence.shows: Comment is stored only if the table exists and the text is non-empty.

statement: Opening a policy source loads the whole comment table from its file at once. A missing file gives an empty table. A missing path, or a failure while reading the file, makes comments unavailable for that source.

evidence.shows: Table loaded, empty if file absent, Nothing on no path or exception.
Conversion to a table can throw on malformed references.
